$comment: The MCP servers this package registers, and where their entry point lives under
node_modules. One list, read by install.mjs when it writes ~/.claude.json and by
doctor.mjs when it checks they are still registered.
It was two lists before, and only one of them existed: the installer's. A server removed
from ~/.claude.json produced no row in the doctor at all, because the doctor enumerated
what WAS registered — the same blind spot the hook check had, in the same shape.
Local command servers only. A server addressed by URL is somebody else's service over the
network and every one of those ends at a login prompt; the doctor reports one as a policy
break, not as a broken install.

A server may be a node entry point under node_modules (`entry`) or a standalone executable this package does not vendor (`bin`). The second kind states where it installs itself and how to put it there, because a manifest that can only describe one shape quietly excludes the other.

playwright.why: the browser every render, audit and motion capture runs in
playwright.note: --headless is not a preference. Its own --help says 'headed by default', so without the flag any browser tool opens a REAL window that takes focus from whatever is fullscreen — reported from a machine where the cursor kept appearing over a game. Everything this package asks a browser for is a render, an audit or a frame capture, and every one of those launches headless already; a person who wants to watch the browser can run the server headed by hand.

context7.why: up-to-date library documentation, so a version-stale API is not invented

codebase-memory-mcp.why: code structure the agent does not have to re-read the tree to learn: index a repo once, then search_graph / trace_path / get_architecture / detect_changes answer in milliseconds instead of a hundred thousand tokens of file-by-file exploration
codebase-memory-mcp.note: MIT, pure C, no language runtime, no API key and no telemetry — its README states it 'makes no network request of its own accord'. IT IS NOT ONE SHARED DAEMON: this file used to say so, and said it as the reason for choosing this over Graft, and it is false. A user-scope MCP server starts once per SESSION, and a machine with six windows open was measured running six of these — so its cheapness per process is the property that matters, not a sharing that does not happen. It is still the right choice (pure C, ~10 MB resident, no runtime, no key), and `settings` below turn off the two things that made six copies expensive. `bin` rather than `entry` because this package does not vendor it: the `mcp` install step downloads the release asset for this platform from `install`, verifies it against the release's checksums.txt, and places the binary where resolveServerBin() reads (LOCALAPPDATA/Programs/<name> on Windows, ~/.local/bin elsewhere).
codebase-memory-mcp.settingsWhy: Worth setting, and NOT the fix — measured. ui_enabled=false drops an HTTP server that all six copies were binding to one port, and auto_watch=false stops a filesystem watcher; index_repository / detect_changes still refresh on demand. But neither quiets the idle CPU: a fresh instance with both off still measured 0.93% of a 24-core machine, against ~1.00% before. That is why registerByDefault is false rather than these settings being treated as a remedy.
codebase-memory-mcp.registerWhy: MEASURED, not assumed. Registered at user scope it starts once per session, and six copies held 4.46% of a 24-core machine — about 1.07 cores — continuously while the machine was idle, for an index of ZERO repositories. Killing them returned 0.87 cores on the spot. It is a busy-poll that config does not quiet: a fresh instance with ui_enabled=false and auto_watch=false still measured 0.93%. So the binary is installed and ready, and registering it is a decision made per project by someone who is actually going to index a repo: claude mcp add codebase-memory-mcp -- "<path to the binary>". The cost of a user-scope server is its idle footprint TIMES the number of open windows, and this one is only worth that when it holds an index.
